profile_text.body:
Credo AI describes itself as an AI governance platform, founded in 2020, that lets enterprises discover AI systems, enforce policies, prove compliance, and manage risk across models, agents, applications, and vendors. The company says it created the AI governance category and now applies the same approach to what it calls Agent Governance, with a registry for agents and agent-specific risk controls. Its platform is built around a Knowledge Graph that combines regulatory intelligence with a customer's business context, and it offers pre-built policy packs covering the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, and other standards. Credo AI also offers GAIA (Govern AI Assistant), which it says is generally available in the platform.

The site states that the company's policy packs were written by a team it says has worked within ISO, NIST, the EU Parliament, NATO, and the OECD, and that the platform draws on more than 300 integrations. Credo AI names Mastercard and IBM in customer and partner statements on its site, including an IBM collaboration on Compliance Accelerators. The site also quotes customers describing faster EU AI Act compliance work and centralized audit support, and says enterprises in insurance, financial services, federal, and healthcare are using the platform.

Beyond the product listing and the 2020 founding year, the records add no litigation, no MCP server, and no SEC or patent facts for Credo AI.
